pages.text: The crafting grid can $(thing)average$() 2–8 compatible tobacco items. This is useful for small lots with different quality values that would not otherwise stack.

pages.title: Crafting Averaging
pages.text: All inputs must be the same tobacco item and compatible processing state. Raw leaf averages with the same raw leaf. Cured leaf must share its cure type. Single-variety loose tobacco must share cure and cut. The result averages occupied crafting slots and rounds down to the whole quality value. This preserves item count while ensuring averaging can never create quality points.

pages.title: Create Homogenization
pages.text: With Create installed, a Mechanical Mixer over a Basin can standardize compatible raw or cured leaves in bulk. A Mixer cycle only starts when its selected batch contains $(thing)at least two different quality values$(). Variety/item and all non-quality processing data must match.

pages.title: Batch Quality
pages.text: Create homogenization uses a $(thing)count-weighted average$() and rounds $(thing)down$() to a whole quality so a Mixer can never manufacture quality points. Every leaf in that Mixer cycle leaves at the same quality. Already-uniform tobacco is not pointlessly remixed.

pages.title: Redstone Batch Control
pages.text: Signal 0 keeps the default $(thing)64-leaf$() target. Power either the $(thing)Mixer or Basin$(); if both are powered, the stronger signal wins. Signals 1–14 select 16/32/48/64/96/128/160/192/256/320/384/448/512/576 leaves.

pages.title: Signal 15: Finish
pages.text: A new rise to signal $(thing)15$() finishes the compatible leaves $(thing)currently inside the Basin$() once, with a 16-leaf minimum. Mixed qualities are homogenized; an already-uniform lot is passed through unchanged. Drop below 15 before issuing another finish command.

pages.title: Continuous Factories
pages.text: Homogenizer input is protected from Chutes, Hoppers, Funnels, and similar extractors until the Mixer processes or flushes it. Repeated same-quality stacks may occupy multiple Basin slots so a later quality can still enter. If all 576 input spaces become full with one quality, that uniform tobacco passes through automatically instead of deadlocking the line.

pages.title: Multi-Stage Homogenizing
pages.text: One Mixer standardizes one physical batch, so a large harvest can leave several nearby qualities. For predictable multi-stage lines, make downstream targets larger than upstream ones: for example 64/128-leaf primary Mixers feeding a 256/576-leaf final Mixer. Pulse 15 to finish the leftover tail.

pages.title: Grading First
pages.text: Create quality Attributes can siphon unusually low or premium leaves away before homogenizing. This lets a factory standardize the normal crop range without sacrificing rare high-quality tobacco or letting extreme low outliers drag down the bulk lot.

pages.title: Averaging vs Crating
pages.text: Homogenizing standardizes quality. Tobacco Crates do not: a full 3×3 grid stores nine units of the same tobacco item losslessly, preserving each unit’s own NBT/components until the crate is broken.
